title: Unsubscribe view ignores the configured user model
reasoning: The notification code elsewhere uses the configured user model, but the unsubscribe view imports django.contrib.auth.models.User directly and looks up the signed user id against that concrete table. In projects with a custom user model, valid unsubscribe links generated for real recipients will fail with User.DoesNotExist and redirect to the error page, leaving users subscribed despite clicking a valid link.
recommendation: Use django.contrib.auth.get_user_model() in notifications/views.py, or import the same configured user model used by the rest of the app before resolving the signed id.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included unsubscribe-related tests generate tokens and inspect email content, but they do not exercise the unsubscribe endpoint with the project's configured user model.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that signs an existing recipient id, calls notifications:unsubscribe, and asserts the recipient profile's receive_promotional_emails flag becomes False and the response redirects to unsubscribe_success.
minimumFixScope: Update notifications/views.py to resolve users via get_user_model() and keep the existing BadSignature, SignatureExpired, and DoesNotExist handling.
